ScoringPolicy: Always require teacher review for geometric drawing, theorem explanation, and graphical interpretation; formula results alone must never yield an overall grade.

Contracts.Title: Weighted averages and common-centre quadrilateral dilation
Contracts.OriginalPrompt: Plot A=(2,3), B=(6,3), C=(8,9), D=(4,9). Partition each segment from A to the other vertex in a 1:4 ratio and draw A,B′,C′,D′. Prove the whole polygon was dilated from A with a common factor, not merely that three coordinates were calculated.

Criteria.Criterion: Label all preimage and image vertices with correct fractions
Identify a single centre and one common scale factor for every vertex
Provide a valid graphical or vector explanation, not only a coordinate list
Explain why differing centres or unequal ratios would not establish one dilation

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Use 4/5 of distance from A rather than 1/5
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Reject ratio reversal and require source convention

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Polygon labelled without coordinates or centre
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Do not auto-grade; ask teacher to clarify evidence

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: A coincides with a second vertex so corresponding segment degenerates
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Review whether geometric proof actually supports a nondegenerate quadrilateral

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Use vector A+(X−A)/5 rather than coordinates listed as fifths
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Accept valid equivalent image with an explicit common-centre argument

Contracts.Title: Sector formulas and the radian slope of an arc-length graph
Contracts.OriginalPrompt: For an original circular-road model with fixed central angle, produce the (radius, arc length) table (2,3),(6,9),(11,16.5),(14,21), plot these ordered pairs with labelled units, explain why line slope is the radian angle, and derive the sector-area formula using the fraction θ/(2π).

Criteria.Criterion: Tabulate all ordered pairs and label axis units accurately
Plot a correctly scaled line through the origin and determine slope by rise/run
Explain slope as radians and justify s=θr, including positive-radius assumptions
Derive area A=(1/2)r²θ from the fraction θ/(2π) and explain square units

IndependentEvidenceOracles.Input: Radius r=20 m under same angle

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Divide radius by arc length and call 2/3 radians the slope

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Use the line's slope; ratio s/r is not defined at zero radius

NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.Trigger: Graph a table of proportional values not exactly the four listed points
NegativeAndEdgeReviewCases.ExpectedHandling: Review mathematical equivalence and clarity before accepting
